questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For producing the effective collisions. the colloiding molecule must posses
options: A certain minimum amount of energy.
Energy equal to or greater than threshold energy.
Threshold energy as well as proper orientation of collision.
questions.solution: Identify the necessary criteria for molecular collisions to result in a reaction. Concept: Collision Theory of Chemical Reactions. Solution: According to Collision Theory, not all collisions between reactant molecules lead to the formation of products; only a small fraction are effective collisions. For a collision to be effective, two primary conditions must be met simultaneously: Energy Factor: The colliding molecules must possess a minimum amount of energy, known as threshold energy (which includes the energy required to overcome the activation energy barrier). Orientation Factor: The molecules must collide in a specific, proper orientation so that existing bonds can break and new bonds can form. If either of these conditions is not satisfied, the molecules simply bounce back without reacting. Rate of Reaction ∝ Number of Effective Collisions. Mathematically: k = P ⋅ Z ⋅ \(e^{−Ea​/RT}\) Here, P represents the orientation (steric) factor and \(e^{−Ea​/RT}\) represents the fraction of molecules with sufficient threshold energy. Final Answer: (D)
